_comment: The sea rising and falling with the moon, and a little puzzle (Jonah, 2026-09-30): the sea is what moves,
but the moon is what moves it, so the tide is the moon's -- a pull (`SkyBodies.PULL`) nothing else sets.
`tidal moon` is the one way to write a tide; it also offers the moon a little larger.
Anywhere else it is only the shore. `tidal sea` is a sea of water, barred rather than leaned (Jonah): a
tidal sea of open air reads as the word failing. `tidal age` bars the sea too and leans the beaches and
the mangroves, and **never reaches the moon** (`unaimed`, nought), so laying it bare does
not solve the puzzle -- a writer who wants the paper tree's window has to work out that the moon is
the thing to aim at. Playtest decides whether nought is too hard.
A moon taken away (`moonless`) leaves the pull nothing to pull with, which is charged mildly.
